2780.t: From Proto-Indo-European *spor-, an o-grade of Proto-Indo-European *sper- (“to strew”). Cognate with σπείρω (speírō, “to sow”), σπέρμα (spérma, “semen, sperm”), and Albanian farë; see σπείρω (speírō) for more.

2791.t: From Proto-Hellenic *skʰíd͏̌d͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *skid-yé-ti, from *skeyd- (“to divide, split”).

2752.t: Of unclear origin: * Many attempts have been made to connect it with Latin fōrma (“form”) (see there for theory of its origin), but the proposed relationship is problematic.

2705.t: Denominal of βλαστός (blastós, “germ, sprout”). Origin uncertain, often compared to either βλωθρός (blōthrós, “tall”), which see, or German Blatt (“leaf, blade”).

2754.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(s)neh₂- (“to flow, to swim”). Cognate with Ναϊάς (Naïás), Νηρεύς (Nēreús), Latin nō, Sanskrit स्नौति (snauti, “to flow; drip”).

2700.t: Probably from Aeolian ζάλευκος (záleukos, “very white”) [with -α-!], from regular Attic δι⁽ά⁾-λευκός [with -ι-, -α-]

2704.t: Uncertain. Beekes proposes a possible pre-form *Βακτήρ (*Baktḗr), which may relate to βάκτρον (báktron) in the same manner as ἀροτήρ (arotḗr) connects to ἄροτρον (árotron).

2799.t: From Proto-Hellenic *téňňō, from Proto-Indo-European *tén-ye-ti, the innovative ye-present of *ten- (“stretch”) (The present tense system includes a *y progressive aspect marker).

2742.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ḱorh₂k-, from *ḱorh₂- (“crow, raven”). Cognates include Latin corvus, cornix.

2775.t: Sometimes suggested to be from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to cut”), but Beekes notes that it is more likely a Pre-Greek loanword instead, with a pre-form along the lines of *karaᵐp-, and possibly related to κάραβος (kā́răbos, “beetle, crustacean”),…

2786.t: From συμπότης (sŭmpótēs, “fellow drinker”) + -ιον (-ĭon), from συμπίνω (sŭmpī́nō, “to drink together”) + -της (-tēs), from συν- (sŭn-, “with, together”) + πίνω (pī́nō, “to drink”).

2774.t: From the radical of σέβομαι (sébomai) + -νός (-nós), with regressive assimilation.

2777.t: Borrowed from a Semitic language, related to Hebrew בָּרֶקֶת (baréket, “emerald, flashing gem”), Akkadian 𒄭𒄭 (barāqum, literally “shining”), Arabic بَرْق (barq, “lightning, flashing, shining, dazzling”) and loanwords of Semitic origin such as Sanskrit मरकत…

2776.t: From Proto-Indo-European *skélos (“curve, bending”), from *(s)kel- (“to curve, bend”).

2790.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(s)gʷʰh₂el- (“to stumble”). Compare Old Armenian սխալեմ (sxalem, “to err”), Sanskrit स्खलति (skhalati, “to stumble”) and possibly Latin fallō.

2756.t: As if from *νουθέτης (*nouthétēs), from νοῦς (noûs) + τίθημι (títhēmi) + -της (-tēs), + -έω (-éō).

2768.t: From πρός (prós, “to, towards, with”) + δοκεύω (dokeúō, “to watch”).

2728.t: A formation like ὄτοβος (ótobos), κόναβος (kónabos) and φλοῖσβος (phloîsbos), likely from the same root as a reduplicated form τονθορύζω (tonthorúzō, “to mumble”), as well as θρῦλος (thrûlos, “murmur”).

2725.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *tʰrəsús, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰr̥sús, from *dʰers-. Cognate with Proto-Slavic *dьrzъ, Sanskrit धृषु (dhṛṣú), and Lithuanian drąsùs.

2721.t: A nu-stem root present from Proto-Indo-European *yewg-. Compare δείκνυμι (deíknūmi, “to show”).

2713.t: δόρυ (dórŭ, “spear, lance”) + φέρω (phérō, “bear, bring, carry”) + -ος (-os, suffix forming two-termination second-declension compound adjectives)

2741.t: Not explained with certainty. The word may be taken as "well-tended hair", in opposition of θρίξ (thríx, “hair”), and connected with κομέω (koméō, “to take care of, tend”).

2709.t: From διαβάλλω (diabállō, “to calumniate”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix).

2753.t: From μύσσομαι (mússomai, “to blow the nose”) + -τήρ (-tḗr). Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *mew-k- (“slip; slime”), the same root of μύκης (mŭ́kēs, “mushroom”), μύξα (mŭ́xă, “mucus; slime”) and Latin mucus.

2783.t: From Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂mn̥ (“that which stands, stature”). Cognate with Latin stāmen and Ancient Greek στάμνος (stámnos, “jar”).

2739.t: From κρέκω (krékō, “to weave”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix). The former is from Proto-Indo-European *krek- (“to weave”), see also Serbo-Croatian kresati, English reel.

2778.t: According to Beekes, probably from the city of Σμύρνα (Smúrna, “Izmir”), itself apparently of unknown origin, and not a by-form of μύρρα (múrrha, “myrrh”).

2764.t: Feminine form of περικεφάλαιος (perikephálaios, “round the head”).

2782.t: From στρέφω (stréphō, “I turn, I twist”) + -τός (-tós, “able to”).

2727.t: From θύρα (thúra, “door”) + the root underlying οὖρος (oûros, “watcher, guardian”) and ἐρύω (erúō, “to protect, guard”).

2714.t: Retrograde formation from δράσσομαι (drássomai, “to grasp, take handfuls”), which is from Proto-Indo-European *dregʰ-.

2740.t: From κρύπτω (krúptō, “hide, conceal”) + -ιος (-ios, “pertaining to, belonging to”)

2729.t: From κατα- (kătă-, “back, downwards”) + βιβάζω (bĭbắzō, “to cause to mount, put on”).
